newsitem.title: USA: China bought 950,000 tonnes soymeal in Q4 - USDA.
newsitem.headline: China bought 950,000 tonnes soymeal in Q4 - USDA.

text.p: China bought 950,000 tonnes of soybean meal during the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with zero purchases the year before, U.S. Agriculture Department chief economist Keith Collins said Monday.
In a speech at USDA's annual Agricultural Outlook Conference, Collins said the activity was nearly eight percent of total world trade purchased in one calendar quarter by one country.
Collins said massive buying by China and a reduced crop in Brazil sapped U.S. soybean stocks, which are projected to be at the lowest level in 20 years by September.
"China's needs now appear to be met, and with record soybean production in both Argentina and Brazil now coming on, U.S. exports are expected to slow during the March-September period," he said.
Collins said in 1997, a modest increase in production coupled with a return to a more typical export level should raise 1997/98 U.S. soybean carryover stocks.
